title: Embedding Rat Heart
author: Shaina Robbins
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w52fg8e

steps.title: Excise and rinse heart
steps.instruction: Immediately after sacrifice, remove the rat heart and rinse it in 1X PBS for 30 seconds to flush blood from the chambers.

steps.title: OCT infiltration of heart
steps.instruction: Place the still‑beating heart in 1X PBS containing 25 % OCT for 1 minute with gentle agitation, then transfer it to 1X PBS containing 50 % OCT for 45 seconds; the heart should remain beating, albeit weaker, allowing OCT to infiltrate the chambers and prevent structural collapse during sectioning.

substeps.instruction: Incubate in 1X PBS + 25 % OCT for 1 min with gentle agitation.
Incubate in 1X PBS + 50 % OCT for 45 s.

steps.title: Position heart in embedding mold
steps.instruction: Place the heart into an embedding mold that already contains a bottom layer of frozen 100 % OCT; ensure the tissue does not sink and that all areas are fully covered with OCT for optimal sectioning.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze the mold
steps.instruction: Suspend the mold with the heart in 100 % OCT in either liquid nitrogen or methanol on dry ice to flash‑freeze it, taking care to avoid any liquid nitrogen or methanol splashing into the mold, which would make the OCT gooey and difficult to section.

substeps.instruction: Choose liquid nitrogen or methanol on dry ice as the cooling medium.
Suspend the mold without allowing the cooling liquid to enter the OCT.

steps.title: Store frozen heart
steps.instruction: Wrap the frozen heart in aluminum foil and plastic wrap, then store it at –80 °C; keep it at –80 °C for at least one day before beginning the sectioning process.
